whatContradictedTheCard: The dispatch's own stated premise -- 'the keyed raster service uses new style paths (rastertiles/<style>)' -- is wrong for the two styles this card actually needed. CARTO's own migration-table documentation (docs.carto.com/faqs/carto-basemaps) maps dark_all to a VECTOR style (dark-matter-gl-style/style.json), not a raster rename; the rastertiles/ prefix belongs only to the separate, newer voyager style family. Ground truth (CartoDB/basemap-styles, the style-list source of truth, plus a live test with the real key) confirms dark_all and light_only_labels keep their EXISTING bare paths -- the actual fix is appending ?key=, nothing else. Acting on the dispatch's stated premise without live-verifying first would have produced a plausible-looking but wrong fix (a rename to paths CARTO does not serve dark_all/light_only_labels under).

A naive HTTP-status check would have missed the original defect entirely: the unkeyed endpoint returns 200 OK with a small watermark PNG, not a 4xx/5xx error. Every verification in this close (CP1's initial diagnosis, CP2's live checks) used byte-count and visual/content comparison, never status code alone.

vercel deploy from inside apps/property-explorer/ failed with a doubled-path error (the project's Root Directory setting gets appended to CWD, not treated as an override) -- corrected by linking and deploying from the repo root instead. Left as a note for whoever next deploys this project via CLI rather than the dashboard.
constraintsHonored: attribution preserved (never removed, verified present in the shipped bundle)

verified MY deployment by bundle marker before declaring done; did not assume the alias pointed at my build without checking
scope held to the two named styles + the env wiring + the deploy; did not fix the leave_behind (hauska-map-style.js's light_all) even though it shares the identical defect

LESSON: Live-verify a vendor's stated migration path before trusting a dispatch's premise about it, even when the premise names a specific, plausible-sounding URL scheme (rastertiles/<style>) -- the dispatch author's own research can be incomplete or point at the wrong part of the vendor's documentation (a vector-migration table, when the actual need was a raster fix).
A watermark served at HTTP 200 is a real, recurring defect-detection trap -- check content, not just status, whenever a vendor might degrade gracefully instead of erroring.

This repo already has a live precedent (VITE_PARCEL_PMTILES_HASH) for reading Vite env vars inside a tsup-compiled package consumed by a Vite app -- worth searching for existing precedent before treating a bundler-interop question as novel/risky.

Vercel CLI's Root Directory handling: deploy from the repo root when a project's dashboard Root Directory setting points into a monorepo subdirectory, not from inside that subdirectory (CWD + Root Directory compose, they do not override each other).
